992118171087117331:
The seventh year of Zhenming, the fifth day of the fifth month
My first venture beyond the mountains was fruitful, and the Elder ordered me to go out again for further training.
They say everyone has their strengths, and mine must lie beyond these peaks. 
The first year of Longde, the sixth day of the fifth month
Only a few months after leaving the mountains, the era name has already changed. How strange.
If I encounter bandits tomorrow, I’ll ask my "old acquaintance" for some news and seize some travel expenses while I’m at it.
The first year of Longde, the seventh day of the fifth month
I waited for my "old acquaintance," but—Wang Qing got to them first!
…No point arguing with such a man. 
The first year of Longde, the eighth day of the fifth month
Met bandits on the road, killed by Wang Qing.
This time, he recognized me as a disciple of the Mo Gate and actually tried to learn defensive tactics from me. Ridiculous.

The first year of Longde, the ninth day of the fifth month
Met bandits on the road, killed by Wang Qing.
Like a shadow, he’s always there—persistent and annoying.

The first year of Longde, the tenth day of the fifth month
Met bandits on the road, and Wang Qing and I ended up fighting. The audacity of this man!
As long as chaos reigns, the arts of the Mohists will have no place. What does an outsider know of our intricate craft? 

The first year of Longde, the eleventh day of the fifth month
No bandits today. Wang Qing brought wine to apologize.
Though the man is irritating, the wine is blameless. Delicious.

The first year of Longde, the twelfth day of the fifth month
Wang Qing brought wine again. This man has too much free time. 

The first year of Longde, the thirteenth day of the fifth month
Wang Qing got drunk and was uncharacteristically quiet. Peaceful.

The first year of Longde, the fourteenth day of the fifth month
Wang Qing got heavily drunk, caressed his sword, and sang a song about "era names." So many changes in just a few decades…
Must’ve been his tears falling into the jar—ruined the wine’s flavor.

The first year of Longde, the fifteenth day of the fifth month
I got heavily drunk. Unfortunately, my studious nature betrayed me—I absentmindedly wrote down defensive tactics while intoxicated.
Hmph, wouldn’t an outsider marvel at such skill? 

The first year of Longde, the sixteenth day of the fifth month
Met bandits on the road, no one else around. Seized two taels and three coins.

In the peaceful years before famine struck, the Zheng family of Da'an stood in great prestige. Kind and generous, the Zheng couple earned the respect of all, aiding neighbors and forging goodwill throughout the community.
Then came the birth of young master Zheng E. The whole town rejoiced—guests from far and wide arrived with gifts, the most precious among them a Gilded Longevity Thread handwoven by his grandmother, symbolizing a full life and a wish for a hundred years of peace and joy. Everyone shared that hope.
Those days were warm and bright, filled with harmony and family. It felt as if such happiness would last forever.
But after the chaos of marauders, Zheng E stood alone in the ruins, watching A'Ruan die before his eyes. His home gone, his family lost. Once surrounded by love, now he was the only one left. Reunion? What a cruel joke. Longevity? Only he had lived.
He untied the golden thread, once a symbol of everyone's hopes, and placed it gently on A'Ruan's grave. The one most wished to live long was gone. As for his own life... he left it there too.
